facts.statement: Dracoraptor fossils were first discovered in 2014 in the Blue Lias Formation on the coast of South Wales.
facts.quote: The fossil was first discovered in 2014 by Rob and Nick Hanigan and Sam Davies at the Blue Lias Formation on the South Wales coast.

facts.statement: The species Dracoraptor hanigani was formally named and described in 2016 by David Martill, Steven Vidovic, Cindy Howells, and John Nudds.
facts.quote: The type species, Dracoraptor hanigani, was named and described in 2016 by British palaeontologists David Martill, Steven Vidovic, Cindy Howells, and John Nudds.

facts.statement: Dracoraptor lived during the Hettangian stage of the Early Jurassic, approximately 201 million years ago, in what is now Wales.
facts.quote: Dracoraptor (meaning "dragon thief") is a genus of coelophysoid dinosaur that lived during the Hettangian stage of the Early Jurassic Period of what is now Wales dated at about 201 million years ago.

facts.statement: The holotype of Dracoraptor is precisely dated to 201.3 million years ago, with a margin of error of ±0.2 million years.
facts.quote: precisely dating the dinosaur to the earliest Hettangian stage, 201.3 million years ago ± 0.2 million years.

facts.statement: Dracoraptor is a genus of coelophysoid dinosaur whose name means "dragon thief".
facts.quote: Dracoraptor (meaning "dragon thief") is a genus of coelophysoid dinosaur

facts.statement: Dracoraptor was a bipedal dinosaur, similar to its relatives.
facts.quote: Dracoraptor was a biped, much like its relatives.

facts.statement: Researchers identified 18 distinguishing traits, or autapomorphies, for Dracoraptor in 2016.
facts.quote: In 2016, 18 autapomorphies (distinguishing traits) were established for Dracoraptor.

facts.statement: Dracoraptor possessed recurved, dagger-shaped teeth with serrated edges containing six to eight denticles per millimeter.
facts.quote: The teeth are recurved or dagger-shaped. The edges of the tooth crown are serrated with six to eight denticles per millimetre (0.03 in).

facts.statement: A furcula, or wishbone, was found in the Dracoraptor fossil, a feature rarely seen in early theropod dinosaurs.
facts.quote: The presence of a furcula was reported. Furculae have only rarely been recovered from early theropod fossils; other examples include those of Segisaurus and Coelophysis.

facts.statement: Dracoraptor was a meat-eater that likely fed on small vertebrate animals, indicated by its small, about one-centimeter-long, pointed and serrated teeth.
facts.quote: Dracoraptor had pointed and serrated teeth, indicating it was a meat-eater. But the teeth were small, about one centimetre long, showing it ate small vertebrate animals.

facts.statement: Due to its small size and long legs, Dracoraptor was likely capable of running at high speeds.
facts.quote: The Dracoraptor would have been able to run at high speeds because of its small size and long legs.

facts.statement: Based on limited ecological data, researchers in 2016 tentatively illustrated Dracoraptor as a shore-dwelling predator and scavenger.
facts.quote: Despite the lack of data regarding its ecology, the authors in 2016 had it tentatively illustrated as a "shore-dwelling predator and scavenger".

facts.statement: Dracoraptor is considered the most basal member of the Coelophysoidea group.
facts.quote: It was the basalmost coelophysoid.

facts.statement: The type species Dracoraptor hanigani was discovered in the Blue Lias Formation in Wales, UK, in March 2014.
facts.quote: La especie tipo, Dracoraptor hanigani, fue descubierta en la Formación Blue Lias en Gales, Reino Unido en marzo del 2014.

facts.statement: Dracoraptor fossils were discovered between 2014 and 2015 near the Welsh village of Penarth.
facts.quote: Los fósiles de Dracoraptor fueron descubiertos entre 2014 a 2015 cerca del pueblo galés de Penarth.

facts.statement: Dracoraptor hanigani was named and described in 2016 by David M. Martill, Steven U. Vidovic, Cindy Howells, and John R. Nudds.
facts.quote: La especie tipo, Dracoraptor hanigani, fue nombrada y descrita en 2016 por David M. Martill, Steven U. Vidovic, Cindy Howells y John R. Nudds.

facts.statement: The genus name combines the Latin word draco, meaning "dragon," referencing the Welsh dragon, with raptor, meaning "thief," a common suffix for theropod names.
facts.quote: El nombre del género combina el término en latín draco, "dragón", en referencia al dragón galés, con raptor, "ladrón", un sufijo usual en los nombres de terópodos.

facts.statement: The species name honors discoverers Nick and Rob Hanigan, though grammatically it should be Haniganorum.
facts.quote: El nombre de la especie es en honor de Nick y Rob Hanigan por ser sus descubridores, aunque para ser gramaticalmente correctos debe ser Haniganorum.

facts.statement: This specimen represents the most complete Mesozoic theropod found in Wales.
facts.quote: Este espécimen representa el terópodo mesozoico más completo hallado en Gales.

facts.statement: Dracoraptor lived at the beginning of the Hettangian, approximately 201.3 million years ago, based on its precise geological layer.
facts.quote: Más exactamente proviene de una capa situada a solo unos metros por debajo de la primera aparición del ammonite jurásico Psiloceras y por sobre los Esquistos Paper que representan la transición litológica del límite Triásico-Jurásico, datando con precisión al dinosaurio a inicios del Hettangiense, hace 201.3 millones de años ± 0.2 millones de años.

facts.statement: Dracoraptor was a bipedal dinosaur.
facts.quote: Dracoraptor era un dinosaurio bípedo.

facts.statement: Dracoraptor had only three teeth in each premaxilla, a basal trait.
facts.quote: Los premaxilares solo tienen tres dientes, un rasgo basal.

facts.statement: The skull had three premaxillary teeth per side and at least seven maxillary teeth.
facts.quote: El cráneo tiene tres dientes premaxilares por lado y al menos siete dientes maxilares.

facts.statement: Dracoraptor's teeth were recurved or dagger-shaped.
facts.quote: Los dientes son recurvados o tienen forma de daga.

facts.statement: The tooth crowns had serrated edges with six to eight denticles per millimeter.
facts.quote: Los bordes de la corona de los dientes están dentados con entre seis y ocho dentículos por milímetro.

facts.statement: The presence of a furcula (wishbone) was reported in Dracoraptor.
facts.quote: La presencia de una furcula fue reportada.

facts.statement: The lower arm bones, ulna, and radius were approximately seven centimeters long.
facts.quote: Los huesos del brazo inferior, el cubito y el radio, tienen una longitud de aproximadamente siete centímetros.

facts.statement: The pubic bone in the pelvis measured 212 millimeters in length.
facts.quote: En la pelvis, el hueso púbico tiene una longitud de 212 milímetros.

facts.statement: The ischial axis was 129 millimeters long, significantly shorter than the pubic axis.
facts.quote: El eje del isquion tiene una longitud de 129 milímetros marcadamente más corta que el eje púbico.

facts.statement: The lesser femoral trochanter was about two-thirds the height of the greater trochanter and separated by a V-shaped notch.
facts.quote: En el fémur, el trocánter menor tiene aproximadamente dos tercios de la altura del trocánter mayor y está separado de él por una hendidura en forma de V.

facts.statement: The third metatarsal in the foot was 116 millimeters long.
facts.quote: En el pie, el tercer metatarso tiene una longitud de 116 milímetros.

facts.statement: Dracoraptor had sharp, serrated teeth indicating it was carnivorous.
facts.quote: Dracoraptor tenía dientes agudos y aserrados, lo que indica que era carnívoro.

facts.statement: Its teeth were small, about one centimeter long, likely for eating small animals.
facts.quote: Pero estos dientes eran pequeños, de cerca de un centímetro de largo, probablemente para comer pequeños animales.

facts.statement: Due to lack of ecological data, 2016 authors tentatively illustrated Dracoraptor as a coastal predator and scavenger.
facts.quote: A pesar de la carencia de datos en lo que respecta a su ecología, los autores de 2016 lo ilustraron tentativamente como un "depredador y carroñero habitante de la costa".

facts.statement: A 2016 cladistic analysis determined Dracoraptor was a basal member of Neotheropoda, near the base of the evolutionary tree.
facts.quote: Un análisis cladístico presentado en 2016 determinó que Dracoraptor era un miembro basal de los Neotheropoda, es decir situado en lo bajo del árbol evolutivo.

facts.statement: Dracoraptor is the most basal known coelophysoid.
facts.quote: Es el celofisoideo más basal conocido.

facts.statement: Pelvis construction indicates Dracoraptor was a saurischian dinosaur.
facts.quote: La construcción de la pelvis muestra que era un dinosaurio saurisquio.

facts.statement: Among dinosaurs, transversely flattened dagger-shaped teeth are found only in Theropoda.
facts.quote: Entre los dinosaurios, los dientes aplanados transversalmente en forma de daga solo se encuentran con Theropoda.

facts.statement: Neotheropoda membership is demonstrated by a superficial depression around the antorbital fenestra, a cranially positioned pleurocoel in neck vertebrae, and an obturator notch in the ischium.
facts.quote: Una pertenencia al clado Neotheropoda se demuestra por la depresión superficial alrededor de la fenestra antorbital, la posición hacia craneal de un pleurocoelo en las vértebras del cuello y la presencia de una muesca del obturador en el isquion.

facts.statement: Dracoraptor's placement in Coelophysoidea is uncertain as it lacks many group synapomorphies, such as a jugal ramus rounded toward the lacrimal.
facts.quote: La posición en Coelophysoidea es más incierta. Dracoraptor no comparte claramente muchas de las sinapomorfias del grupo, como una rama de yugal redondeada hacia el lagrimal.

facts.statement: Dracoraptor is the oldest dinosaur found in Wales.
facts.quote: Dracoraptor es el más antiguo dinosaurio encontrado en Gales.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen NMW 2015.5G.1–2015.5G.11 was found in the lower Bull Cliff Member of the Blue Lias Formation in the UK.
facts.quote: El espécimen holotipo, NMW 2015.5G.1–2015.5G.11, fue descubierto en la zona inferior del Miembro Bull Cliff de la Formación Blue Lias del Reino Unido.

facts.statement: The genus Dracoraptor was named by Martill and colleagues in 2016.
facts.quote: PBDB name: Dracoraptor (genus), Martill et al. 2016

facts.statement: Dracoraptor belongs to the parent group Coelophysoidea.
facts.quote: Parent group: Coelophysoidea

facts.statement: Dracoraptor is classified within the class Reptilia.
facts.quote: Class: Reptilia

facts.statement: Dracoraptor lived during the Hettangian stage, between 201.4 and 199.5 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Hettangian to Hettangian (201.4 to 199.5 million years ago)

facts.statement: Only one fossil occurrence of Dracoraptor has been recorded in the database.
facts.quote: Fossil occurrences recorded: 1
